 From this we can work out the vehicle speed:-

 Given that that tyres on the Polestar 2 are 245/45 R19, their circumference = 220.756cm

 220.756cm = 0.001371527778 miles

 2554 RPM = 153240 RPH (Revolutions per hour)

 Whilst online documentations seems to suggest that the Polestar 2 (LRDM) has a 8.57:1 ratio drive, I believe that it is actually ~9.1:1

 153240 / 9.1 * 0.001371527778 miles = 23.09MPH

 

 Working on this, the top speed of the Polestar 2 = 14,000RPM (840000 RPH) 

 840000 / 9.1 * 0.001371527778 = 126.6 MPH

 

 If the ratio of 8.57 is to be believed then the car either has a top speed of 134.43MPH or the motor is limited to 13250 RPM

Can-IDLengthDATA Packet HEXDATA Packet DECIMALRegister Description

 | 8

 | 222 189 071 043 164 144 192 009
 | 400V Battery Voltage (V) / Current(A)
 | 
 

 
 

 Please note that there are some assumptions here, I do not entirely know how the battery management is done in the Polestar2.

 

 Battery voltage (V)

 

 Battery Voltage is 10 bits on bytes 0 & 1

 There appears to be a 2.5V offset per cell . This is then divided by 4.32

 

 Example for 82% battery capacity.

 Byte [0,1] = [0xDE,0xBD] = 0xDEBD = 1101111010111101b = 701(dec) = (701/4.32)+270 = 432V (4.00V per cell) 

 

 Example for 100% and 5% capacity. 

 100% = CF,0A = 1100111100001010b = 778 = (778/4.32)+270 = 450V (4.16V per cell)

 5% = DD,C7 = 1101110111000111b = 455 = (455/4.32)+270 = 375V (3.47V per cell)

 To work out this equation I logged the charge voltages from a Fastned 300KW charger during a fast charge.

 I guess the 270 offset equates to an offset of 2.5V per cell (2.5V being the cut off voltage for a lithium cell)

 2.5* 108 cells = 270

 (108 cells being the number of cells in the Dual Motor, Long range battery pack)

 I have measured the following Charge / Discharge curves on my car:-

 

 * Discharge of 0.136C = (Energy consumption of 32KW/100miles at ~32MPH average).

 

 Battery Current (A)

 

 Battery Current is 15 bits on bytes 6 & 7

 This is centred at 0x4000 (16384) and then divided by 10

 

 Example with zero current draw

 Byte [6,7] = [0xC0,0x00] = 0xC000 = 1100000000000000b = 16,384(dec) = (16,384-16,384)/10 = 0A 

 
 Example for very heavy acceleration.

 Byte [6,7] = [0xD0,0x3E] = 0xD03E = 1101000000111110b = 20,542(dec) = (16,384-20,542)/10 = -415.8A 

 
 Example with regen.

 Byte [6,7] = [0xB7,0x41] = 0xB741 = 1011011101000001b = 14,145(dec) = (16,384-14,145)/10 = +223.9A
